title: Functions in Tables and Mapping Diagrams Core Test
description: Identify inputs, reason about unique outputs, and explain representations and counterexamples.

questions.questionText: A table lists x -> y as 11 -> 2, 12 -> 4, 13 -> 6. Is the displayed relation a function?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes; every listed x has one y.
questions.explanation: Read the input column first. Each listed input has one assignment, so these rows define a function on the listed inputs.
options: Yes; every listed x has one y.
No; the y-values are different.
No; x does not start at zero.
Yes; every table is a function.

questions.questionText: A mapping shows arrows 11 -> 5 and 11 -> 9. Which input has conflicting outputs?
questions.explanation: Follow the arrows from 11: one goes to 5 and one to 9. One input with two different outputs fails the test.

questions.questionText: Three arrows are 11 -> 8, 12 -> 8, 13 -> 8. Do converging arrows break the function rule?
questions.correctAnswer: No; each input still has just one outgoing assignment.
questions.explanation: Several arrows may end at the same output. The test concerns arrows leaving each input, not arriving at each output.
options: Yes; an output can receive only one arrow.
No; each input still has just one outgoing assignment.
Yes; the output must increase.
No; every arrow diagram is a function.

questions.questionText: Read the table: input 11 gives 3; input 12 gives 6; input 13 gives 9. What is the output for input 12?
questions.explanation: Find the specified input row and read its paired output. Do not use the input number itself as the answer.

questions.questionText: The stated input set is {11, 12, 13}. Arrows are shown only from 11 and 12. What is missing for a function on that entire input set?
questions.correctAnswer: One output assignment for 13.
questions.explanation: A function must assign an output to every input in its stated domain, as well as avoiding conflicting outputs.
options: A different output for every input.
A second arrow from every input.
One output assignment for 13.
An arrow from every output back to an input.

questions.questionText: A table contains (11, 2), (12, 5), (11, 2). A student rejects it because x repeats. What is the correction?
questions.correctAnswer: The repeated x has the same y both times, so the displayed relation is a function.
questions.explanation: Identical rows repeat the same assignment. Only different outputs for the same input create a conflict.
options: The repeated x must be deleted even when its output agrees.
It is not a function because every y must be different.
It is a function only if the inputs are sorted.
The repeated x has the same y both times, so the displayed relation is a function.
